Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone thanks for carving out the hour and a bit today. we wanted to focus on the outstanding contract friction and the implementation window so we can align procurement and legal expectations.
[00:22] Lena: thanks. main thing for us is the SLA piece. Averton operates 24/7 customer-facing workflows — we need clarity for p99 and an acceptable remediation path if redwould (Redwood) misses targets. also DPA exceptions around data deletion and sub-processor notif — those are the main redlines.
[00:45] Marcus: and from procurement side, we need firm pricing for reserved capacity with commit levels, and a path if we need to scale up mid-term. charges for egress and KMS also must be baked in.
[01:05] Priya M: understood. quick caveat — the tech bench we ran last week showed dedicated pools get about 35% lower per-token cost at our prompt mix but you trade some latency predictability if you over-burst. i'll share the sheet.
[01:27] Dr. Gao: small correction — latency predictability is actually better on dedicated, hosted had some variance. can priya send the raw logs? we want to look at tail lat percentiles.
[01:46] Priya M: yes i'll include p50/p95/p99 and KV cache -- sorry K-V cash -- hit patterns. expect a spreadsheet.
[02:05] Lena: about SLA wording: Averton legal will not accept a pure best-effort clause. can we map Redwood's internal SLOs to contractual SLA and include credits or escalation steps?
[02:25] Ethan: absolutely. typical path is to have a monetary credit tied to monthly uptime below the threshold. for Dedicated we can push to 99.95 with credits; for hosted we generally guarantee 99.5 with automated fallback to a compatible model variant. can we talk concretely about the remediation timelines you need?
[02:50] Lena: we need a 48-hour remediation plan for severity-1 incidents and a defined on-call escalation matrix. also requirement for audit logs for every token request at least for a rolling 30-day window.
[03:12] Olivia: we can provide token-level tracing and a per-route log export; retention can be extended as an add-on. for audit logs we may need to discuss retention and cost.
[03:28] Priya Raman: on security: we insist on customer-managed KMS for key custody of PII-derived embeddings. does Redwood support BYOK/HSM?
[03:45] Ethan: yes, we support both Redwood-managed KMS and BYOK via standard KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). for HSM-level custody we have a private deployment option; there are costs and a slightly longer provisioning window.
[04:05] Marcus: provisioning window — how long to stand up a private deployment vs dedicated in our region? we have compliance windows to meet for Q2 go-live.
[04:23] Priya M: private VPC/on-prem takes about 6-8 weeks from signed P.O. for the standard package (air-gapped package a bit longer). Dedicated reserved pools typically 2-3 weeks. we can compress timelines with a paid expedite.
[04:45] Marcus: procurement will want that in writing. also need a cancellation/termination penalty schedule so we can model our budget.
[05:00] Ethan: we'll add termination and early-exit fees into the MSA cleanly; often negotiable based on commit duration.
[05:18] Lena: on DPA, our data team flagged subprocessors list — we need at least 30 days notice before Redwood adds a new subprocessor and the right to audit.
[05:35] Ethan: standard we notify, but 30-day notice is reasonable. audit rights often limited to SOC2 reports and on-site audits for enterprise plans. we can surface SOC2 Type II and any ISO artifacts.
[05:48] Priya Raman: also around data residency: some of our EU customers require European-only processing. is regional pinning available?
[06:04] Priya M: yes, regional pins via Dedicated or Private. Hosted has region affinity but not guaranteed hard pin unless you opt for Private.
[06:18] Dr. Gao: quick tech question — in a failover scenario you mentioned 'compatible model variant' as fallback. what is the model behavior change? any prompt drift or embedding re-ingest required?
[06:34] Priya M: fallbacks are to the same family but a quantized variant; outputs are generally comparable but slight statistical drift can occur. we recommend a canary and perf-test of critical prompts. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles that minimize quality regression.
[06:56] Marcus: back to pricing: can you outline how reserved capacity discounts change with commit tiers? we need to show 12 vs 24 month scenarios.
[07:10] Ethan: short answer: 12-month commit gives X% discount, 24-month gives additional Y%. i'll share a tiered pricing sheet. also note that dedicated reduces per-token compute but there are fixed monthly infra fees.
[07:30] Lena: one more legal ask — indemnification carveouts for regulated data and export controls. we have to ensure Redwood's MSA aligns with our export compliance program.
[07:46] Ethan: we can add standard indemnities; for export controls we will need to align with your compliance team on restricted data flows.
[08:00] Olivia: i'm going to drop links in the follow-up: security pack (SOC2 + ISO links), standard SLA language examples, and a sample redline that other customers have used.
[08:14] Marcus: please include any egress pricing examples; our finance team is particularly sensitive to data transfer fees.
[08:25] Priya M: egress is usually per-GB and depends on region; dedicated customers often have negotiated egress buckets as part of the commit. we'll model both common and worst-case.
[08:40] Lena: regarding the redline, what parts of the MSA are non-negotiable for Redwood? we need to know up front to avoid a lot of back-and-forth.
[08:55] Ethan: non-negotiables generally include export of logs for 3rd parties that compromise privacy, and some of the fundamental product terms (intellectual property ownership). but SLA thresholds, termination windows, and data retention are commonly negotiated. we'll mark the MSA sections as flexible vs core.
[09:15] Dr. Gao: can we carve out a short pilot window where we can run a POC for 4 weeks to validate inference quality and tail latency on our traffic patterns before full commit?
[09:28] Ethan: yes, a pilot is standard. typical pilot terms: 30-day pilot with limited commit and baseline pricing; if you convert to a commit within 30 days of pilot end, some pilot fees can be credited.
[09:47] Marcus: procurement will need a demo of billing visibility — does the Redwood Console provide token-level cost breakdowns for routes and token types?
[10:00] Olivia: yes Console shows token-level cost, per-route breakdown, and you can roll up by team. we can provide a read-only view for your finance users.
[10:12] Priya Raman: auditability — where do logs live and who can access them? we need strict RBAC; can we map roles to SSO groups?
[10:26] Ethan: yes SSO+SAML integration and RBAC mapping to groups is supported. for private deployments we can do custom RBAC tied to your IdP.
[10:40] Lena: quick note — we will insist on a clause for 3rd party subprocessors that they comply with our DPA terms.
[10:52] Ethan: understood. we'll add that language with standard mutual obligations.
[11:05] Marcus: timeline check — if we sign P.O. on 2026-02-18, what's realistic for production-ready in EU + US?
[11:18] Priya M: with Dedicated in two regions, about 3-4 weeks after PO for baseline; Private would be more like 6-8 weeks. depends on KMS onboarding and network build.
[11:33] Lena: then procurement wants to see the redline by 2026-02-10 to hit internal signoff.
[11:42] Ethan: we'll aim for that. I'll send redline and a one-page summary of differences + SLA mapping.
[11:52] Olivia: i'll attach the security pack and a sample pricing scenario. Priya will share bench logs.
[12:00] (overlap/crosstalk) Dr. Gao: and the bench should include tail lat across our prompt set — the last time we saw a spike at p99 that broke timeouts.
[12:12] Priya M: will do. note: we'll include both hosted and dedicated runs and the quantized variants.
[12:25] Lena: one more item — can Redwood accept a limited on-site audit if needed? sometimes for high-risk flows we need vendor audits.
[12:36] Ethan: on-site audits are possible for enterprise agreements; we'll note the process and estimated lead time.
[12:45] Marcus: ok i think we covered the high-level items. next steps again — redline by 2/10, bench by 2/9, Averton to confirm procurement attendees by 2/12.
[12:59] Ethan: great. i will follow up with a calendar invite for a decision meeting the week of 2/15. thanks all.
